feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of scope, progression, and technical breadth. It reads professionally and is largely polished, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in digital platform modernization, governance, analytics, and communications operations.  
- Good credibility signals: internal promotion history, named employer, large-scale metrics, and concrete platforms/tools make the profile believable and senior.  
- Broad but relevant skill mix: combines leadership, technical execution, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia in a way that fits modern digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a tighter structure and more space for achievements.  
- Strengthen impact language: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes; add more measurable results beyond platform size/audience figures.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; punctuation/hyphenation varies (“organization-wide” vs. other compounds, “A2/Learning,” “10×20-foot”); “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler in Education.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening the language and adding one sharper differentiator would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct outcome-oriented language: “leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and analytics for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Combines editorial, technical, and multimedia leadership to deliver scalable, user-centered digital experiences, including AI-enabled search and discovery.”
- Use parallel structure: “web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia operations.”
- Keep “AI-enabled” but narrow it to “search and discovery” for specificity and consistency with recent projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The list of capabilities repeats core competencies almost verbatim; the intro should synthesize, not enumerate.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased as broader capability areas rather than repeating near-identical wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; e.g., use concise noun phrases throughout.
- Consider a cleaner version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for specificity and clearer alignment with the AI search project.
- Change “operations”/“systems” repetition where possible to improve rhythm and reduce generic wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; if space is tight, shorten or remove one of those sections.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” in Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it feel more additive and polished.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise, parallel bullet for easier scanning.
- Strengthen specificity with outcomes, audience, or scale where possible (for example, campaign reach, stakeholder group, or operational value).
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong, but other entries could be more concise and active.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider prioritizing similarly unique projects here to avoid repeating core job duties.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the “Recent Projects” section. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or adoption signals.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-focused statements, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and member-facing resource toolkits.”
- “Improved communications operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content models, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”
- “Provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.”
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording duplicates the footer project summaries; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the examples.
- “Governance/usability/operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope-and-impact summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize biggest wins first: website migration, analytics infrastructure, video studio, then governance/operations.
- Tighten channel bullet and add outcomes if available: open/click rates, audience growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance.
- Use stronger action/result phrasing, e.g., “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this at a higher strategic level here.
- Video expansion may partially duplicate older NACo entries unless framed as building enterprise studio capacity and in-house production infrastructure.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier digital/media role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership language.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector platforms”
- Make the list more distinctive and concise, e.g.:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Audience-centered content strategy and campaign planning
- Consider dropping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” unless messaging is a target-role priority; it reads less differentiated than governance/operations leadership.
- If space allows elsewhere, move proof points like “10,000+ page migration” or “3.5M annual page views” into experience bullets rather than skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets on editorial planning and coordination.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work: Drupal-led modernization, integrations/automation, and AI-enabled search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”
- De-emphasize older or lower-signal items here; move WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, and jQuery to “Technical + IT” only.
- Replace “technical execution” phrasing with impact-oriented language if space allows: “Enterprise web delivery” or “Platform modernization & integrations.”
- If you want one proof point, add a brief qualifier: “Drupal platform leadership for 10,000+ page public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating all three verbatim elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and decision-making impact over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten wording and elevate outcomes: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; use Topline Skills for strategic strengths, not a second software list.
- “SEO and performance analysis” is close to “performance optimization”; choose one phrasing for consistency.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and aligned to recent leadership-level multimedia work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Tighten and elevate phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations**

- Keep this section focused on capability areas; leave software/tool names (e.g., Premiere Pro, Audition) in Technical + IT

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; consider shortening one or removing the overlap.
- “Studio operations” and “Livestream studio workflows” partially duplicate Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level and recency, e.g.: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, prioritize most relevant platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but Drupal should clearly lead given recent experience.
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS Platforms” for concision.
- Best stronger version: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere; consider dropping it if space is tight.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, front-end troubleshooting, and CMS implementation support
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent work
- If space allows, add one proof point in a nearby project/role instead of here, e.g., “used to support Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and lightweight workflow automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere, so don’t imply GitHub Actions duplicates that category unless you specify CI/CD or deployment support

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame around automation/orchestration.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by relevance/technical depth: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp”
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If you’ve built notable automations, consider replacing one lower-value collaboration tool with a qualifier: “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate, Zapier…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; if space is tight, they’re weaker than automation/project systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS consistency: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter and campaign automation
- Keep newest/most enterprise-relevant platform first; if Dynamics was the primary recent system, preserve that order.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “campaign management” language here if those points are already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo roles.
- Don’t repeat automation terminology already listed under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you specify email-specific automation.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a generic list rather than a differentiated technical capability section. Tighten it and emphasize tools over broad concepts.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • Google Optimize/experiment platforms
- Replace broad terms like “SEO,” “A/B testing,” and “Dashboarding” with specific platforms or methods only if you actually used named tools.
- If no additional tools are available, shorten the heading or list to avoid padding; the impact already appears in the 2022–2024 NACo role.
- Keep ordering aligned to strongest/recent evidence: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider deleting one or making this version tools-only and the topline version outcomes/methods-focused.
- “SEO” also overlaps with broader strategy language elsewhere; avoid repeating it unless tied to a specific platform or analysis capability.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it read as the foundation-building phase: team formation, early channel operations, and concrete production contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcomes where possible: website refresh support, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the closing clause to show light management: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored a junior digital staff member.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles, helping launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while providing day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy research initiatives for NACo programs and helped expand digital storytelling efforts.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and stress ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a clearer action, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia content supporting program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid leaning too heavily on general digital content/video language already covered in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t repeat “supporting organizational programs and policy work” if similar policy/advocacy support appears elsewhere; keep this entry focused on innovation projects + first podcast launch.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it will make the section feel more technical and less duplicative.

Suggested edit
- Reframe as tools first, then production specialties: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast editing/production”
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with a cleaner, more standard phrase like “Livestream production” or “Studio production workflows.”
- If accurate, add one higher-value tool or platform tied to recent work (for example, streaming/recording software or studio systems) rather than generic capabilities.
- Keep this item concise; let work experience carry the impact, and reserve this line for recognizable tools and production domains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Podcast production” overlaps with older 2013–2015 experience; keep it only if still relevant to current positioning.
- Multimedia/livestreaming already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, so avoid repeating broad phrasing here.
